questions.q: What's the core difference between a parameter and a variable in SSIS?
options: A parameter feeds a value into a package from the outside at execution time; a variable holds state the package manages internally while it runs
There is no real difference — they're interchangeable terms for the same feature
A variable can only hold numbers; a parameter can hold any data type
Parameters only exist inside Execute SQL Tasks
questions.explain: Parameters let you modify how a package executes without opening and editing it — variables are internal state the package itself manages at run time.

questions.q: Where do you create a project parameter, and how does its visibility differ from a package parameter?
options: In the Project.params file — a project parameter is usable by any package in the project, unlike a package parameter, which only that one package can use
On the Parameters tab of each individual package — identical to a package parameter
In the Variables window
Project parameters aren't created in SSDT at all; they only exist after deployment
questions.explain: Project parameters live in one shared Project.params file and are visible to every package in the project, while package parameters are scoped to the single package whose Parameters tab created them.

questions.q: A parameter is marked Required and has a design default of 5. After the project is deployed with no server value set, what happens if you try to run it with no execution value either?
options: The package fails to execute — a server or execution value must be supplied for a required parameter once deployed
The package runs using the design default of 5
The parameter silently resets to 0
SSIS prompts interactively for a value
questions.explain: Marking a parameter Required means the design default alone isn't enough once the project is deployed — a server value or an execution value must be present, or the package won't execute.

questions.q: If a project parameter has a Design Value of 1, a Server Value of 5, and no Execution Value is set for a given run, what value is actually used?
options: 5 — the server value overrides the design value whenever no more specific execution value is supplied
1 — the design value always wins
SSIS averages the two values
The run fails because two values are set
questions.explain: Execution values override server values, which override design values — with no execution value set, the server value of 5 is what's used.

questions.q: What does marking a parameter as Sensitive actually do?
options: Encrypts its value in the SSISDB catalog, so it appears as NULL when viewed with T-SQL or SSMS
Hides the parameter from the Parameters tab entirely
Prevents the parameter from ever being changed after deployment
Makes the parameter visible only to sysadmins in SSMS, but still shows the real value
questions.explain: A Sensitive parameter's value is encrypted in the catalog and reads back as NULL through T-SQL or Object Explorer — the right setting for a password or API key.
